questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the elements of an assurance engagement?

options.A: A three-party relationship between the practitioner, the responsible party and the intended users
options.B: Suitable criteria against which the subject matter is evaluated
options.C: A written assurance report containing the practitioner's conclusion
options.D: A guarantee from the practitioner that the subject matter is free from fraud

questions.explanation: An assurance engagement has five elements: a three-party relationship, an appropriate subject matter, suitable criteria, sufficient appropriate evidence and a written assurance report. No assurance engagement provides a guarantee, and absolute assurance about the absence of fraud is never possible. The other three options are all recognised elements.

questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: In the statutory audit of a UK limited company, which party is the 'responsible party' in the three-party relationship?

options.A: The company's directors
options.B: The company's shareholders
options.C: The audit engagement partner
options.D: The Registrar of Companies

questions.explanation: The responsible party is the party responsible for the subject matter, which for financial statements is the directors who prepare them. The shareholders are the intended users, and the audit partner represents the practitioner. The Registrar simply receives the filed accounts and is not a party to the engagement.

questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: Which of the following wordings would be typical of the conclusion in a limited assurance engagement?

options.A: In our opinion, the information is prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the criteria
options.B: Based on our procedures, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the information is not prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the criteria
options.C: We certify that the information is free from all error and fraud
options.D: We confirm that every transaction underlying the information has been checked and found to be correct

questions.explanation: Limited assurance is expressed in a negative form: the practitioner states that nothing has come to their attention suggesting the information is materially misstated. A positive 'in our opinion' conclusion is used for reasonable assurance engagements such as an audit. No assurance engagement certifies freedom from all error, and procedures are never performed on every transaction.

questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: What is the main reason why the shareholders of a large company need an independent audit of its financial statements?

options.A: Shareholders are legally responsible for preparing the financial statements and need help to do so
options.B: Ownership is separated from management, so shareholders need independent assurance on information prepared by the directors who run the business
options.C: An audit guarantees that the company will pay a dividend
options.D: An audit allows shareholders to avoid having to read the financial statements themselves

questions.explanation: In most large companies the shareholders do not manage the business, so the directors act as their agents and prepare financial statements reporting on their own stewardship. Because directors may have incentives to present results favourably, an independent audit adds credibility to the information. Directors, not shareholders, prepare the statements, and an audit gives no guarantee about dividends.

questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT an inherent limitation of an audit?

options.A: Much of the audit evidence available is persuasive rather than conclusive
options.B: The financial statements are prepared under a recognised financial reporting framework
options.C: The auditor usually tests a sample of items rather than the whole population
options.D: Internal controls can be overridden by management or circumvented by collusion

questions.explanation: Inherent limitations mean an auditor can give only reasonable, not absolute, assurance. They include the persuasive nature of evidence, the use of sampling and judgement, and the possibility of management override or collusion. Preparing the statements under a recognised framework is a precondition for an audit rather than a limitation, because it provides suitable criteria.

questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: Which of the following public perceptions is an example of the 'expectation gap' in auditing?

options.A: The directors are responsible for preparing the financial statements
options.B: An unmodified audit opinion means the financial statements are guaranteed to be completely accurate
options.C: The auditor provides reasonable assurance rather than absolute assurance
options.D: The auditor's report is addressed to the company's members

questions.explanation: The expectation gap is the difference between what users believe auditors do and what auditors actually do. Believing that an audit guarantees complete accuracy is a common misunderstanding, because an audit provides reasonable assurance only and materiality means small errors may remain. The other three statements are accurate descriptions of the audit.

questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: Which of the following engagements is NOT an assurance engagement?

options.A: A review of a listed company's interim financial information
options.B: An examination of a client's profit forecast for a bank loan application
options.C: Preparing a client's VAT return from its accounting records
options.D: The statutory audit of a company's annual financial statements

questions.explanation: Preparing a VAT return is a compilation or tax service: the accountant prepares information but does not evaluate it against criteria or express a conclusion. Reviews of interim information, examinations of prospective financial information and statutory audits all involve the practitioner gathering evidence and giving a conclusion to intended users, so they are assurance engagements.

questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about an agreed-upon procedures engagement is correct?

options.A: The practitioner expresses a limited assurance conclusion on the subject matter
options.B: The practitioner chooses the procedures to perform based on an assessment of risk
options.C: The practitioner reports factual findings and the users draw their own conclusions from them
options.D: The practitioner gives reasonable assurance because the procedures are agreed in advance

questions.explanation: In an agreed-upon procedures engagement the practitioner performs procedures agreed with the engaging party and reports what was found. No conclusion is expressed, so no assurance is given and the engagement is not an assurance engagement. The procedures are set by agreement, not by the practitioner's own risk assessment.

questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: A small company is exempt from statutory audit but its directors are considering a voluntary audit. Which of the following is a genuine benefit of a voluntary audit?

options.A: Lenders and suppliers may place greater reliance on the financial statements when deciding whether to extend credit
options.B: Responsibility for the financial statements transfers from the directors to the auditor
options.C: The audit guarantees that the company will continue as a going concern
options.D: The company no longer needs to keep adequate accounting records

questions.explanation: An independent audit adds credibility to the financial statements, which can help when negotiating finance or credit terms; the auditor may also highlight control weaknesses. The directors remain responsible for the financial statements and for keeping accounting records whether or not there is an audit. An audit does not guarantee the future viability of the business.

questions.topic: The concept of and need for assurance
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly compares reasonable assurance and limited assurance engagements?

options.A: Engagement risk is eliminated entirely in a reasonable assurance engagement
options.B: Engagement risk is reduced to a lower level in a reasonable assurance engagement, so the procedures performed are generally more extensive
options.C: A limited assurance engagement requires more evidence because its conclusion is expressed negatively
options.D: Both types require the same procedures and differ only in the wording of the report

questions.explanation: In a reasonable assurance engagement the practitioner reduces engagement risk to an acceptably low level, which requires more extensive evidence and supports a positive opinion. In a limited assurance engagement the risk is higher, the procedures (often inquiry and analytical review) are more restricted and the conclusion is negative. Risk can never be eliminated completely.

questions.question_text: Under the Companies Act 2006, who normally appoints the auditor of a UK company on an ongoing basis?

options.A: The board of directors
options.B: The company secretary
options.C: The shareholders (members)
options.D: The audit committee of the audit firm

questions.explanation: Auditors are normally appointed by the members, for example by ordinary resolution at a general meeting of a public company. Directors may appoint the first auditors or fill a casual vacancy, but the ongoing appointment rests with the members. This supports the auditor's independence from the directors on whose statements they report.

questions.question_text: A prospective auditor asks a potential new client for permission to contact the existing auditor. The client refuses. What should the prospective auditor do?

options.A: Decline the appointment
options.B: Accept the appointment but contact the existing auditor anyway
options.C: Accept the appointment and perform extra substantive procedures to compensate
options.D: Ask the Registrar of Companies whether there are any reasons not to accept

questions.explanation: Professional clearance requires the prospective auditor to seek the client's permission to communicate with the existing auditor. A refusal without good reason suggests the client may be hiding something, so the prospective auditor should decline. Contacting the existing auditor without permission would breach confidentiality, and extra testing cannot replace the information sought.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of an audit engagement letter?

options.A: To confirm in writing the agreed terms of the engagement, including the responsibilities of the auditor and of management
options.B: To report significant deficiencies in internal control to those charged with governance
options.C: To set out the detailed audit procedures and sample sizes for the year
options.D: To provide the auditor's opinion on the financial statements

questions.explanation: The engagement letter records the agreed terms of the audit, such as its objective and scope, the respective responsibilities of auditor and management, the framework used and the form of reports expected. This reduces the risk of misunderstanding. Control deficiencies are reported separately, detailed procedures are in the audit plan, and the opinion is in the auditor's report.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would normally be included in an audit engagement letter?

options.A: The auditor's assessment of materiality for the year
options.B: Management's responsibility for preparing the financial statements and for internal control
options.C: A list of the items to be selected for testing
options.D: The internal control deficiencies the auditor expects to find

questions.explanation: Engagement letters set out the agreed terms, including management's acknowledgement of its responsibilities for the financial statements, internal control and giving access to information. Materiality and sample selections are planning judgements that are not shared in advance, otherwise the audit could become predictable. Deficiencies cannot be known before the audit work is performed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a precondition for an audit?

options.A: The company has no history of material misstatements
options.B: The auditor has already completed a full risk assessment
options.C: The company's internal controls have been confirmed as effective
options.D: Management agrees that it is responsible for giving the auditor access to all relevant information and people

questions.explanation: The preconditions for an audit are the use of an acceptable financial reporting framework and management's agreement to its responsibilities, including providing access to information. The auditor confirms these before accepting the engagement. A history of errors or weak controls affects risk assessment but does not prevent an audit, and the risk assessment happens after acceptance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors would most likely cause an audit firm to decline a new audit engagement?

options.A: The client has been trading for only two years
options.B: The client's year end is the same as many of the firm's other clients
options.C: The client wants a fee estimate before the engagement is agreed
options.D: The firm has no staff with experience of the client's specialised industry and cannot obtain such staff in time

questions.explanation: A firm should accept work only if it has the competence, capabilities and resources to perform it properly, so a lack of relevant expertise is a strong reason to decline. A young business, a busy year end or a request for a fee estimate are normal commercial matters that can be managed. Accepting work outside the firm's competence would breach the principle of professional competence and due care.

questions.question_text: Before accepting a new audit client, which of the following does the firm have to do under UK anti-money laundering requirements?

options.A: Obtain a credit rating report to confirm the client can pay the audit fee
options.B: Make a precautionary report about the client to the National Crime Agency
options.C: Identify the client and verify its identity, including identifying its beneficial owners
options.D: Obtain confirmations of all bank balances directly from the client's bank

questions.explanation: Customer due diligence requires firms to identify the client and verify its identity on reliable independent evidence, including who ultimately owns or controls it, before establishing the business relationship. Making a report without any suspicion is not required. Credit checks and bank confirmations may be useful but are not anti-money laundering requirements.

questions.question_text: A prospective auditor receives a reply from the existing auditor, with the client's permission, saying that the directors have previously given misleading information to the auditors. What should the prospective auditor do?

options.A: Ignore it, since the existing auditor may simply be reluctant to lose the client
options.B: Report the directors immediately to the police
options.C: Accept the appointment but tell the directors what the existing auditor said
options.D: Consider this information carefully when deciding whether to accept the appointment, as it raises doubts about management integrity

questions.explanation: Professional clearance exists so that the prospective auditor learns of matters relevant to accepting the appointment. Concerns about management integrity increase the risk of the audit significantly and may lead the firm to decline. The information should not be dismissed, nor passed to the directors, and misleading the auditors is not by itself a matter for police reporting.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT an objective of planning an audit?

options.A: To ensure that the financial statements contain no material misstatements
options.B: To help the auditor give appropriate attention to important areas of the audit
options.C: To help identify and resolve potential problems on a timely basis
options.D: To help assign team members with suitable skills to each area

questions.explanation: Planning helps the auditor focus on the key risk areas, deal with problems early, organise the engagement and allocate staff with appropriate skills. However, planning cannot ensure that there are no material misstatements; the directors are responsible for the financial statements, and the auditor gives only reasonable assurance.

questions.question_text: Audit risk is a function of inherent risk, control risk and detection risk. Which of these can the auditor directly influence?

options.A: Detection risk
options.B: Inherent risk
options.C: Control risk
options.D: Both inherent risk and control risk

questions.explanation: Inherent risk and control risk are risks of material misstatement that exist within the entity, independently of the audit; the auditor assesses them but cannot change them. Detection risk is the risk that the auditor's procedures fail to detect a material misstatement. The auditor manages it through the nature, timing and extent of substantive procedures.

questions.question_text: An auditor has assessed both inherent risk and control risk for trade receivables as high. What is the appropriate response?

options.A: Plan more extensive substantive procedures on receivables to reduce detection risk
options.B: Reduce substantive procedures on receivables, because the risk has already been identified
options.C: Rely on tests of controls only, as controls are the main source of risk
options.D: Increase materiality for receivables to make misstatements less significant

questions.explanation: To keep audit risk at an acceptable level, a high risk of material misstatement must be offset by low detection risk. The auditor achieves this through more, and more persuasive, substantive procedures, for example larger samples or procedures closer to the year end. High control risk means controls cannot be relied upon, and raising materiality would be an inappropriate response.

questions.question_text: An audit firm sets overall materiality at 5% of profit before tax. A client's draft profit before tax is £840,000. What is overall materiality?
questions.explanation: Overall materiality = 5% x £840,000 = £42,000. £84,000 would be 10% of profit, £4,200 would be 0.5% and £21,000 would be 2.5%. The benchmark and percentage are a matter of judgement, and the auditor would revise materiality if the final profit figure changed significantly.

questions.question_text: Overall materiality for an audit is £60,000. The firm sets performance materiality at 75% of overall materiality and treats misstatements below 5% of overall materiality as clearly trivial. What is performance materiality?
questions.explanation: Performance materiality = 75% x £60,000 = £45,000. It is set below overall materiality to reduce the risk that uncorrected and undetected misstatements together exceed overall materiality. £15,000 is the 25% difference, £3,000 is the clearly trivial threshold (5% x £60,000) and £80,000 wrongly divides £60,000 by 0.75.

questions.question_text: Which of the following misstatements is most likely to be material by its nature, even though the amount is small?

options.A: A small error in the depreciation charge on office furniture
options.B: A minor cut-off error in sales of a few hundred pounds
options.C: An understatement of directors' remuneration disclosed in the notes to the financial statements
options.D: A small misclassification between two categories of administrative expenses

questions.explanation: Materiality has qualitative as well as quantitative aspects. Directors' remuneration is of particular interest to shareholders and is a legal disclosure, so even small errors may influence users and reflect on directors' stewardship. Small, routine errors in depreciation, cut-off or expense classification are unlikely to be material unless their size is significant.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most likely to indicate a high inherent risk?

options.A: The client holds a large inventory of fashion clothing whose saleability depends on changing trends
options.B: The client does not separate the duties of recording and banking cash receipts
options.C: The audit team has no experience of the client's industry
options.D: The audit sample sizes have been reduced to meet a reporting deadline

questions.explanation: Inherent risk is the susceptibility of a balance to misstatement before considering controls. Fashion inventory may become obsolete quickly, making its valuation at the lower of cost and net realisable value subjective. Poor segregation of duties is a control risk, while inexperienced staff and reduced samples increase detection risk.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes control risk?

options.A: The risk that the auditor's procedures will fail to detect a material misstatement
options.B: The risk that the auditor expresses an inappropriate opinion when the financial statements are materially misstated
options.C: The risk that a misstatement that could be material will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis by the entity's internal control
options.D: The susceptibility of an assertion to material misstatement before considering any related controls

questions.explanation: Control risk relates to the entity's own internal control failing to prevent or detect and correct a misstatement. The auditor's failure to detect misstatements is detection risk, and expressing an inappropriate opinion is audit risk overall. The susceptibility of an assertion before controls is inherent risk.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of performing analytical procedures at the planning stage of an audit?

options.A: To help identify unusual changes or relationships that may indicate risks of material misstatement
options.B: To provide sufficient appropriate evidence on all account balances
options.C: To replace the need for any tests of detail
options.D: To confirm the arithmetical accuracy of the trial balance

questions.explanation: Analytical procedures are required as risk assessment procedures because they help the auditor understand the entity and highlight balances that are out of line with expectations. These areas can then be targeted for further work. They are not designed at planning to provide substantive evidence or to check arithmetic.

questions.question_text: A client's credit sales for the year were £3,650,000 and its trade receivables at the year end were £450,000. Last year receivables collection was 30 days. Assuming a 365-day year, what is this year's collection period and what risk does it suggest?

options.A: 45 days; trade receivables may be overstated because of irrecoverable debts
options.B: 45 days; trade receivables may be understated because of unrecorded sales
options.C: 30 days; there is no change in risk from the prior year
options.D: 22 days; the allowance for receivables may be overstated

questions.explanation: Receivables days = £450,000 / £3,650,000 x 365 = 45 days. The increase from 30 to 45 days suggests customers are paying more slowly, so some balances may not be recoverable and receivables could be overstated if no adequate allowance is made. A longer collection period does not suggest understatement.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a risk assessment procedure used to obtain an understanding of the entity and its environment?

options.A: Making inquiries of management and others within the entity
options.B: Performing analytical procedures
options.C: Sending confirmation requests to the client's major customers
options.D: Observing operations and inspecting documents such as board minutes

questions.explanation: Risk assessment procedures comprise inquiries, analytical procedures, and observation and inspection. External confirmations of customer balances are further audit procedures performed in response to assessed risks, to provide evidence about receivables. They are not used to gain an understanding of the entity.

questions.question_text: A client's revenue has risen by 10% while its cost of sales is unchanged, so the gross margin has risen from 30% to 38%. The business has not changed its pricing or suppliers. Which risk is this most likely to indicate?

options.A: Purchases may be incomplete, or closing inventory may be overstated
options.B: Revenue may be understated
options.C: Closing inventory may be understated
options.D: Administrative expenses may be overstated

questions.explanation: With unchanged prices and suppliers, cost of sales should rise roughly in line with revenue. An unchanged cost of sales may mean purchases have been omitted or closing inventory overstated, both of which reduce cost of sales and inflate the margin. Understated revenue or understated inventory would lower the margin, and administrative expenses do not affect gross margin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be included in the detailed audit plan rather than the overall audit strategy?

options.A: The overall scope of the engagement and the reporting deadlines
options.B: The broad direction of the audit and the areas of highest risk
options.C: The specific procedures to be performed on trade receivables, including sample sizes
options.D: The resources to be allocated to the audit, including the use of specialists

questions.explanation: The audit strategy sets the scope, timing and direction of the audit and the resources needed. The audit plan is more detailed, setting out the nature, timing and extent of the specific procedures to be performed, such as the tests on receivables and their sample sizes.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a component of an entity's system of internal control?

options.A: The control environment
options.B: The entity's risk assessment process
options.C: The external auditor's substantive procedures
options.D: Control activities

questions.explanation: The components of internal control are the control environment, the entity's risk assessment process, its process to monitor internal control, the information system and communication, and control activities. The external auditor's procedures are part of the audit, not part of the entity's own internal control.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: Which of the following forms part of the control environment?

options.A: The attitude of those charged with governance towards internal control
options.B: Monthly bank reconciliations
options.C: Passwords restricting access to the sales ledger
options.D: Sequential numbering of sales invoices

questions.explanation: The control environment includes the governance and management functions and their attitudes, awareness and actions concerning internal control, including commitment to integrity and ethical values. Bank reconciliations, passwords and sequential numbering are specific control activities that operate within that environment.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a detective control rather than a preventive control?

options.A: Authorisation of purchase orders before they are sent to suppliers
options.B: Monthly reconciliation of purchase ledger balances to supplier statements
options.C: Restricting physical access to the inventory store
options.D: Checking a customer's credit limit before accepting an order

questions.explanation: A detective control identifies errors or irregularities after they have happened, so that they can be corrected. Reconciling supplier statements reveals differences already recorded in the ledger. Authorising orders, restricting access and credit checks all operate before the transaction or event, so they are preventive.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: Which of the following combinations of duties shows the most serious lack of segregation of duties?

options.A: One employee prepares sales invoices and another posts them to the receivables ledger
options.B: One employee orders goods and another checks them on delivery
options.C: One employee both receives customer cheques and maintains the receivables ledger
options.D: One employee prepares the payroll and the finance director authorises the payment

questions.explanation: Good segregation separates custody of assets from recording of the related transactions. An employee who handles cheques and maintains the receivables ledger could steal receipts and conceal it by manipulating customer accounts, for example by teeming and lading. The other combinations involve two different people at the key stages.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an IT general control?

options.A: Regular back-up of data, with copies stored securely off-site
options.B: Check digit verification on customer account codes
options.C: Batch totals agreed before and after processing
options.D: A range check that rejects weekly hours above a set maximum

questions.explanation: General IT controls apply to the whole IT environment, for example back-ups, access security, program development and change controls. Check digits, batch totals and range checks are application controls, which relate to the input, processing and output of a particular application.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: A computerised sales system performs a sequence check on sales invoice numbers. What is the main purpose of this control?

options.A: To ensure that invoices are calculated at the correct prices
options.B: To ensure that sales are only made to customers who are creditworthy
options.C: To identify missing or duplicated invoice numbers, supporting the completeness of recorded sales
options.D: To ensure that invoices are posted to the correct customer accounts

questions.explanation: A sequence check looks for gaps and duplicates in a numbered sequence, so it helps ensure that every invoice raised is recorded once only. Pricing accuracy relies on controls over price lists, credit risk is controlled by credit checks, and correct posting is supported by controls such as check digits on account codes.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: Two cheque signatories, each required to approve every payment, agree together to sign payments to a fictitious supplier they have set up. Which inherent limitation of internal control does this illustrate?

options.A: Collusion
options.B: Management override
options.C: Human error
options.D: Controls designed for routine transactions only

questions.explanation: The control of two signatories relies on each acting independently. When two or more people agree to act together to circumvent the control, it is collusion, which internal control cannot fully prevent. Management override occurs when a manager instructs others to bypass controls, and human error involves mistakes rather than deliberate fraud.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a test of control?

options.A: Inspecting a sample of purchase invoices for evidence of approval by the purchasing manager
options.B: Agreeing a sample of payables ledger balances to supplier statements
options.C: Recalculating the year-end accrual for electricity
options.D: Comparing this year's wages expense with last year's

questions.explanation: Tests of control obtain evidence about whether controls operated effectively during the period, such as looking for evidence that invoices were approved. Agreeing balances to supplier statements, recalculating accruals and comparing wages year on year are substantive procedures that seek evidence directly about the amounts.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: How should an auditor communicate significant deficiencies in internal control identified during an audit?

options.A: Orally to the accounts clerk responsible for the relevant area
options.B: In the opinion section of the auditor's report
options.C: In writing to those charged with governance on a timely basis
options.D: Only when the shareholders ask about internal control at the annual general meeting

questions.explanation: Auditing standards require significant deficiencies to be communicated in writing to those charged with governance on a timely basis. Other deficiencies may be reported to management at an appropriate level. Control weaknesses do not by themselves modify the auditor's opinion, which concerns the financial statements.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: Which of the following would NOT normally be included in an auditor's report to management on internal control deficiencies?

options.A: A description of each deficiency found
options.B: An explanation of the possible effects of each deficiency
options.C: A recommendation for improving each control
options.D: A statement that the auditor has identified all of the deficiencies in the company's internal control

questions.explanation: A report on deficiencies normally sets out each deficiency, its possible consequences and a recommendation. It also explains that the audit was not designed to identify all deficiencies, because the auditor considers controls only to the extent needed to design audit procedures. Claiming to have found all deficiencies would be misleading.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: Which of the following controls best prevents unauthorised changes being made to a company's accounting software?

options.A: Program changes are tested and approved by users and IT management before being moved into the live environment
options.B: Data input is checked using validity and range checks
options.C: Hash totals are calculated on batches of payroll data
options.D: The cash book is reconciled to the bank statement each month

questions.explanation: Program change controls are general IT controls designed to ensure that only authorised, tested changes are made to live programs. Validity checks, range checks and hash totals are application controls over data rather than programs. A bank reconciliation is a manual detective control over cash.

questions.topic: Internal control systems and IT controls
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of a walk-through test?

options.A: To confirm the auditor's understanding of the system by following a transaction through it from start to finish
options.B: To provide substantive evidence for the year-end balance
options.C: To test whether a control operated effectively throughout the year
options.D: To select a statistical sample of transactions for testing

questions.explanation: In a walk-through test the auditor traces one or a few transactions through the system to confirm that it operates as documented, for example in flowcharts or narrative notes. It is not enough to show that controls worked throughout the period, which requires tests of control on a sample, and it does not provide substantive evidence on balances.

questions.question_text: Which control best reduces the risk of sales being made to customers who are unlikely to pay?

options.A: Sales invoices are sequentially numbered
options.B: Credit limits are set for each customer and checked before an order is accepted
options.C: Monthly statements are sent to customers
options.D: Goods despatched notes are signed by the customer

questions.explanation: Setting and checking credit limits before accepting orders prevents the company from supplying customers who are a poor credit risk. Sequential numbering supports completeness, statements help detect errors in customer accounts, and signed despatch notes provide evidence of delivery. None of these addresses creditworthiness before the sale.

questions.question_text: Which control best ensures that all goods despatched to customers are invoiced?

options.A: Sales invoices are checked by a second person for arithmetical accuracy
options.B: Customer orders are checked against approved credit limits
options.C: Goods despatched notes are sequentially numbered, matched to sales invoices, and the sequence is checked for gaps
options.D: Sales invoices are authorised by the sales manager before being sent

questions.explanation: Matching sequentially numbered despatch notes to invoices and investigating gaps helps ensure that every despatch results in an invoice, which supports the completeness of revenue. Checking arithmetic addresses accuracy, credit checks address recoverability, and authorising invoices addresses occurrence and pricing.

questions.question_text: A company sends statements to all credit customers each month. Which risk does this control mainly address?

options.A: Errors or misappropriations in customers' ledger accounts going undetected
options.B: Goods being supplied to customers without a credit check
options.C: Sales being recorded in the wrong accounting period at the year end
options.D: Sales invoices being raised for goods that have not been ordered

questions.explanation: Customers who receive statements are likely to query balances that are too high, so errors, or the misappropriation of payments, are more likely to be detected. The control works best when statements are prepared and sent by someone independent of the receivables ledger and cash. It does not address credit checks, cut-off or unauthorised invoicing directly.

questions.question_text: Which control best reduces the risk that credit notes are used to conceal the theft of customer receipts?

options.A: Credit notes are posted to the receivables ledger on the day they are raised
options.B: Credit notes are filed alphabetically by customer name
options.C: Credit notes are issued only by the receivables ledger clerk
options.D: Credit notes are sequentially numbered and authorised by a manager independent of cash receipts and the receivables ledger

questions.explanation: An employee who steals receipts might issue fictitious credit notes to clear the customer's balance. Requiring independent authorisation and accounting for the sequence of credit notes makes this more difficult. Posting promptly or filing by customer does not prevent fraudulent credit notes, and allowing the ledger clerk to issue them alone increases the risk.

questions.question_text: At a client, the sales clerk who raises sales invoices can also change the prices held in the system's standing data. What is the main risk arising?

options.A: Goods may be despatched without a despatch note being raised
options.B: Sales may be made to customers who exceed their credit limits
options.C: Invoices may be raised at unauthorised prices, causing misstated revenue or enabling fraud
options.D: Customer receipts may be posted to the wrong customer account

questions.explanation: Changes to standing data such as price lists affect every subsequent transaction, so they should be authorised by a senior person independent of invoicing. A clerk who can change prices and raise invoices could undercharge favoured customers or make errors that go unnoticed. The other risks relate to despatch, credit and cash allocation controls.

questions.question_text: In a purchases system, which three documents are typically matched before a supplier invoice is approved for payment?

options.A: The purchase order, the goods received note and the supplier invoice
options.B: The purchase requisition, the remittance advice and the bank statement
options.C: The sales order, the goods despatched note and the sales invoice
options.D: The supplier statement, the cheque stub and the purchase day book

questions.explanation: Matching the purchase order, the goods received note and the supplier invoice confirms that the goods were authorised, actually received, and invoiced at the agreed price and quantity. The other combinations involve documents relating to payment, sales, or recording rather than approval of the invoice.

questions.question_text: Which control best ensures that the company records liabilities only for goods it has actually received?

options.A: Supplier invoices are matched to goods received notes before being posted to the payables ledger
options.B: Purchase orders are authorised by the department manager
options.C: Supplier statements are reconciled to the payables ledger each month
options.D: Payments to suppliers require two authorised signatories

questions.explanation: Matching invoices to goods received notes confirms that goods were received before the liability is recorded, supporting the occurrence of purchases. Authorising orders controls what is ordered, not what is received. Supplier statement reconciliations are detective controls, and dual signatories control payments rather than the recording of liabilities.

questions.question_text: Which control best reduces the risk of payments being diverted by changing a supplier's bank details?

options.A: Supplier invoices are checked for arithmetical accuracy
options.B: The payables ledger is totalled and reconciled to the control account monthly
options.C: Goods received notes are checked against purchase orders
options.D: Changes to supplier bank details must be authorised by a senior manager and verified with the supplier using contact details already on file

questions.explanation: A common fraud involves false requests to change a supplier's bank details, so payments go to a fraudster. Independent authorisation of master file changes and verification with the genuine supplier using known contact details helps prevent this. The other controls relate to invoice accuracy, ledger integrity and receipt of goods, not standing data.

questions.question_text: At the year end, a company reviews all goods received notes that have not yet been matched to supplier invoices and accrues for them. Which assertion does this control mainly address?

options.A: Existence of trade payables
options.B: Valuation of inventory
options.C: Occurrence of purchases
options.D: Completeness of trade payables and accruals

questions.explanation: Goods received before the year end but not yet invoiced are liabilities at the year end. Reviewing unmatched goods received notes ensures these liabilities are recorded, which addresses completeness. Existence and occurrence concern whether recorded items are genuine, and inventory valuation concerns the lower of cost and net realisable value.

questions.question_text: Which of the following controls does NOT help to ensure the completeness of trade payables?

options.A: Supplier invoices are checked for arithmetical accuracy before being posted
options.B: Supplier statements are reconciled to payables ledger balances each month
options.C: The sequence of goods received notes is checked and missing numbers investigated
options.D: Goods received but not invoiced are reviewed at the year end

questions.explanation: Completeness concerns whether all liabilities that should be recorded have been recorded. Reconciling supplier statements reveals invoices the company has not recorded, sequence checks on goods received notes identify receipts not processed, and the year-end review identifies uninvoiced receipts. Checking arithmetic addresses the accuracy of invoices already received, not whether any are missing.

questions.question_text: Which control best reduces the risk of a supplier invoice being paid twice?

options.A: Invoices are marked as paid when settled, and the system rejects duplicate invoice numbers for the same supplier
options.B: Purchase orders are sequentially numbered
options.C: Goods received notes are signed by the storekeeper
options.D: Supplier invoices are filed in date order

questions.explanation: Cancelling invoices once paid and having the system reject duplicate invoice references prevents the same invoice being processed twice. Numbering purchase orders and signing goods received notes relate to ordering and receipt, not payment. Filing in date order does not stop a duplicate being processed.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: Which control best reduces the risk of fictitious ('ghost') employees being added to the payroll?

options.A: Payslips are given to employees in sealed envelopes
options.B: The payroll is totalled and cross-cast each month
options.C: Employees clock in using a swipe card
options.D: Additions to the payroll master file are authorised by the HR department, independently of the payroll staff

questions.explanation: A ghost employee is created by adding a fictitious person to the payroll so that their pay can be diverted. Requiring independent HR authorisation for new joiners prevents payroll staff from adding employees themselves. Sealed payslips, casting checks and clocking-in do not stop someone being added to the master file.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: Which control best reduces the risk of hourly paid staff being paid for hours they did not work?

options.A: Net pay is paid directly into employees' bank accounts
options.B: Payroll deductions are reconciled to amounts paid to HM Revenue & Customs
options.C: Pay rates are reviewed annually by the board
options.D: Clocking-in is supervised and timesheets are approved by the employee's supervisor before payroll processing

questions.explanation: Supervised clocking-in prevents one employee clocking in for another, and supervisor approval of timesheets confirms that the hours recorded were worked. Paying by bank transfer, reconciling deductions and reviewing rates are useful controls but do not address whether the hours claimed are genuine.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: Which control best ensures that PAYE income tax and National Insurance deducted from employees are correctly paid over to HM Revenue & Customs?

options.A: New employees must provide evidence of their identity to HR
options.B: The payroll department checks that pay rates agree with employment contracts
options.C: A monthly reconciliation of deductions per the payroll to amounts paid to HM Revenue & Customs, reviewed by the finance manager
options.D: Overtime is approved by the department manager

questions.explanation: Reconciling the tax and National Insurance shown on the payroll with the amounts paid each month helps ensure the liability is paid correctly and on time, and that the year-end balance owed is accurate. The other controls relate to the validity of employees, pay rates and overtime rather than payment of deductions.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a physical control over inventory?

options.A: Inventory records are updated daily from goods received and despatch notes
options.B: Inventory is kept in a locked store with access restricted to authorised staff
options.C: Slow-moving inventory reports are reviewed by the purchasing manager
options.D: Inventory count sheets are sequentially numbered

questions.explanation: Physical controls safeguard assets directly, for example locks, secure stores and restricted access. Updating records, reviewing slow-moving items and numbering count sheets are controls over recording, valuation and the count process rather than physical protection of the inventory.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: During a year-end inventory count, count sheets are sequentially numbered, issued to count teams and accounted for at the end of the count. What is the purpose of this control?

options.A: To ensure that inventory is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value
options.B: To ensure that damaged inventory is identified
options.C: To ensure that only goods owned by the company are counted
options.D: To ensure that all count sheets are returned, so that no counted inventory is omitted

questions.explanation: Accounting for the sequence of count sheets ensures that none are lost or that extra ones are added, so the final inventory listing includes everything counted. Valuation, damaged items and ownership are addressed by other procedures, such as reviewing costs, recording condition during the count and segregating goods held for third parties.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: A client uses a perpetual inventory system with continuous counting instead of a full year-end count. Which of the following would be necessary for the auditor to rely on this system?

options.A: Only high-value items are counted, and only at the year end
options.B: Counts are performed by the storekeeper, who maintains the inventory records
options.C: All inventory lines are counted at least once a year and discrepancies with the records are investigated and corrected
options.D: Differences between counts and records are left uncorrected until the following year

questions.explanation: Continuous counting can replace a year-end count if the book records are reliable. This requires all items to be counted during the year, counts to be performed by staff independent of the records and stores, and differences to be investigated and corrected. Counts by the storekeeper or leaving errors uncorrected would undermine reliance on the records.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: Which of the following controls mainly addresses the valuation of inventory, rather than its existence or completeness?

options.A: Test counts from the inventory records to the physical items in the warehouse
options.B: Matching goods received notes to the inventory records
options.C: Regular review of inventory ageing reports, with old or slow-moving lines considered for write-down
options.D: Restricting access to the warehouse to authorised staff

questions.explanation: Inventory must be measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value, so slow-moving or obsolete lines may need writing down. Ageing reviews identify these items, which addresses valuation. Counts from records to the warehouse address existence, matching goods received notes addresses completeness, and access restrictions safeguard the inventory.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of a company preparing a monthly bank reconciliation that is reviewed by someone independent of the cash book?

options.A: To ensure all customers pay on time
options.B: To detect errors or irregularities in the cash book or on the bank statement on a timely basis
options.C: To authorise payments to suppliers
options.D: To prevent cash from being stolen before it is banked

questions.explanation: A bank reconciliation compares the cash book with the bank statement and explains differences, such as timing items, so errors and unauthorised transactions can be identified and corrected. Independent review increases its effectiveness. It is a detective control and does not authorise payments or prevent theft before banking.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: Which control over cash received in the post is most effective?

options.A: Post is opened by the receivables ledger clerk, who records receipts directly in the ledger
options.B: Post is opened by two people together, who list all receipts on a remittance list before passing them for banking
options.C: Cheques received are kept in an unlocked drawer until a full week's receipts have accumulated
options.D: Remittance advices are discarded once the cheques have been banked

questions.explanation: Having two people open the post and immediately list receipts reduces the risk of theft and provides an independent record to agree to the banking and the cash book. Letting the ledger clerk handle receipts combines custody and recording, keeping cheques unsecured increases the risk of loss, and discarding remittances removes useful evidence.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: Which of the following describes an imprest system for petty cash?

options.A: Petty cash is topped up whenever the cashier requests it, without supporting vouchers
options.B: A fixed float is held, and it is topped up periodically by the total of the vouchers for amounts spent
options.C: All petty cash received from sales is held in the tin until the year end
options.D: Petty cash expenditure is recorded only once a year when the float is counted

questions.explanation: Under an imprest system, cash plus vouchers should always equal the fixed float, so differences can be easily detected. The float is replenished by the value of vouchers presented, which supports the authorisation and recording of petty cash expenditure. Top-ups without vouchers or annual recording would make it impossible to control.

questions.topic: Controls over payroll, inventory and cash
questions.question_text: Which of the following controls is most likely to detect 'teeming and lading' by a receivables clerk?

options.A: Cash received is banked daily
options.B: Customer statements are sent by someone independent of cash receipts and the receivables ledger, who also follows up customer queries
options.C: The cash book is totalled by the cashier at the end of each day
options.D: Sales invoices are sequentially numbered

questions.explanation: Teeming and lading involves stealing a receipt from one customer and concealing it by allocating later receipts from other customers to that account. Customers whose payments have been delayed in being allocated may query their statements, and an independent person following up queries is likely to detect the fraud. Daily banking, casting the cash book and numbering invoices do not reveal misallocations.

questions.question_text: In the context of audit evidence, what do the terms 'sufficient' and 'appropriate' refer to?

options.A: Sufficient refers to the quality of evidence, and appropriate refers to its quantity
options.B: Sufficient means all items have been tested, and appropriate means the client agrees
options.C: Sufficient refers to the timing of evidence, and appropriate refers to its cost
options.D: Sufficient refers to the quantity of evidence, and appropriate refers to its quality (relevance and reliability)

questions.explanation: Sufficiency is the measure of the quantity of audit evidence, which is affected by risk and by the quality of the evidence. Appropriateness is the measure of quality, meaning its relevance and reliability in supporting the auditor's conclusions. The two are interrelated: higher quality evidence may mean less is needed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sources of audit evidence about a company's bank balance is the most reliable?

options.A: A photocopy of the year-end bank statement provided by the client
options.B: A confirmation sent by the bank directly to the auditor
options.C: An oral statement from the finance director about the balance
options.D: A client-prepared bank reconciliation

questions.explanation: Evidence obtained directly by the auditor from an independent external source is generally the most reliable. A photocopy supplied by the client could have been altered, oral statements are less reliable than written evidence, and a client-prepared reconciliation is generated internally. The bank reconciliation still needs testing, but the confirmation provides the strongest evidence of the balance.

questions.question_text: An auditor selects items from the client's inventory records and physically inspects them in the warehouse. Which assertion does this procedure mainly test?

options.A: Completeness
options.B: Existence
options.C: Valuation
options.D: Classification

questions.explanation: Testing from the records to the physical items checks that recorded inventory actually exists. Testing in the opposite direction, from the physical items to the records, tests completeness. Physical inspection may give some evidence of condition, but valuation is mainly tested by examining costs and selling prices.

questions.question_text: During an inventory count, the auditor selects items on the warehouse floor and traces them to the final inventory listing. Which assertion is being tested?

options.A: Existence
options.B: Completeness
options.C: Rights and obligations
options.D: Accuracy

questions.explanation: Starting with the physical items and checking they appear in the records tests whether all inventory that exists has been recorded, which is completeness. Testing from the records to the floor would test existence. Ownership and accuracy require evidence such as purchase invoices and cost records.

questions.question_text: Which of the following procedures best tests the cut-off of sales?

options.A: Agreeing a sample of sales invoices to customer orders
options.B: Sending confirmation requests to customers with the largest balances
options.C: Comparing monthly sales with the budget
options.D: Selecting goods despatched notes from shortly before and after the year end and checking the related sales were recorded in the correct period

questions.explanation: Cut-off concerns recording transactions in the correct accounting period. Examining despatches around the year end and checking when the related sales were recorded identifies items recorded in the wrong period. Agreeing invoices to orders tests occurrence, confirmations test existence of receivables, and budget comparisons are analytical procedures that are less precise.

questions.question_text: An auditor obtains an official copy of the title register from HM Land Registry for a freehold property owned by a UK client. Which assertion does this mainly support?

options.A: Valuation
options.B: Rights and obligations
options.C: Completeness
options.D: Cut-off

questions.explanation: The title register shows who owns the property, so it provides evidence that the entity holds the rights to the asset. It does not show the property's value, which would require evidence such as a valuation report or depreciation calculations. It also does not show whether all properties have been recorded.

questions.question_text: An auditor compares the cost of a sample of year-end inventory items with their selling prices after the year end. Which assertion is being tested?

options.A: Existence
options.B: Completeness
options.C: Occurrence
options.D: Valuation

questions.explanation: Inventory must be measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Comparing cost with post year-end selling prices, less costs to sell, shows whether any items need writing down below cost. This does not test whether the items exist or whether all items are recorded.

questions.question_text: An auditor reviews the repairs and maintenance expense account for items that should have been capitalised as property, plant and equipment. Which assertion about property, plant and equipment does this mainly test?

options.A: Existence
options.B: Rights and obligations
options.C: Completeness
options.D: Cut-off

questions.explanation: If capital expenditure has been charged wrongly to repairs, property, plant and equipment will be understated. Searching the expense account for such items therefore tests whether all assets have been recorded. Existence would be tested by inspecting assets on the register, and rights by examining ownership documents.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about written representations from management is correct?

options.A: They are the most reliable form of audit evidence because they are signed by the directors
options.B: They can replace other audit evidence that the auditor would otherwise obtain
options.C: They are necessary audit evidence but do not on their own provide sufficient appropriate evidence about the matters they cover
options.D: They are optional and need only be obtained if the client offers them

questions.explanation: Auditing standards require written representations, for example that management has fulfilled its responsibilities and provided all relevant information. However, they come from the entity itself, so they cannot replace other evidence that should be available. If management refuses to give required representations, the auditor must consider the effect on the opinion.

questions.question_text: An auditor finds that evidence from a customer confirmation is inconsistent with the client's records. What should the auditor do?

options.A: Accept the client's records, as they are prepared by the entity's accounting system
options.B: Accept the confirmation and adjust the financial statements without further work
options.C: Determine what changes or additions to audit procedures are needed to resolve the matter, and consider the effect on other aspects of the audit
options.D: Ignore the inconsistency if the difference is below performance materiality

questions.explanation: When evidence from different sources is inconsistent, the auditor must investigate further, for example by reviewing the customer account, cut-off and cash received, to find the cause. The inconsistency may indicate errors or fraud that also affect other areas. Neither source should simply be accepted, and individually small differences may still matter in aggregate or reveal a systematic problem.

questions.question_text: An auditor uses an independent property valuer as an auditor's expert. Which of the following is the auditor required to do?

options.A: Refer to the expert in an unmodified auditor's report to share responsibility for the opinion
options.B: Accept the expert's conclusions without evaluation, as the expert has specialist skills
options.C: Obtain the client's approval of the expert's findings before using them
options.D: Evaluate the expert's competence, capabilities and objectivity, and the adequacy of the expert's work

questions.explanation: When using an auditor's expert, the auditor must evaluate whether the expert has the necessary competence, capabilities and objectivity, agree the scope of the work and evaluate whether the findings are adequate. The auditor retains sole responsibility for the opinion, so an unmodified report does not refer to the expert. Client approval is not required.

questions.question_text: An auditor watches the client's staff carrying out the year-end inventory count. What type of audit procedure is this?

options.A: Inspection
options.B: Inquiry
options.C: Observation
options.D: Reperformance

questions.explanation: Observation consists of looking at a process or procedure being performed by others, such as watching the inventory count. Inspection involves examining records, documents or physical assets, inquiry involves seeking information from people, and reperformance involves the auditor independently carrying out a control.

questions.question_text: An auditor independently prepares the client's year-end bank reconciliation to check that the client's control has operated correctly. What type of procedure is this?

options.A: Recalculation
options.B: Observation
options.C: External confirmation
options.D: Reperformance

questions.explanation: Reperformance is the auditor's independent execution of procedures or controls originally performed by the entity, such as a bank reconciliation. Recalculation checks the mathematical accuracy of documents or records, observation involves watching a process, and external confirmation is a direct response from a third party.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes a positive confirmation request for trade receivables?

options.A: The customer is asked to reply only if they disagree with the balance
options.B: The customer is asked to reply in all cases, either agreeing the balance or providing details of any differences
options.C: The customer is asked to send a copy of their payment to the auditor
options.D: The auditor telephones the customer to confirm the balance orally

questions.explanation: A positive confirmation asks the customer to respond whether or not they agree, which provides more reliable evidence because a reply is expected. A negative confirmation asks for a reply only if the customer disagrees, so a non-reply provides limited evidence. Oral confirmations are less reliable than written responses received directly.

questions.question_text: A customer does not reply to a positive confirmation request for its year-end balance, even after a follow-up. Which alternative procedure is most appropriate?

options.A: Treat the balance as confirmed because the customer did not dispute it
options.B: Remove the balance from the sample and select a different customer
options.C: Ask the client's credit controller to confirm the balance in writing
options.D: Inspect cash received from the customer after the year end and agree it to remittance advices for invoices outstanding at the year end

questions.explanation: When no reply is received to a positive request, the auditor should perform alternative procedures. Cash received after the year end for specific invoices is strong evidence that the debt existed. A non-reply cannot be treated as agreement, replacing the item would bias the sample, and a confirmation from the client's own staff is internal evidence.

questions.question_text: Last year a client's total wages cost was £1,200,000 for an average of 40 employees. This year the average number of employees is 44 and all staff received a 3% pay rise from the first day of the year. What is the auditor's expected wages cost for this year?
questions.explanation: Average cost per employee last year = £1,200,000 / 40 = £30,000. After the 3% rise: £30,000 x 1.03 = £30,900. Expected cost = £30,900 x 44 = £1,359,600. £1,320,000 ignores the pay rise, £1,236,000 ignores the extra employees, and £1,356,000 wrongly adds the 3% and 10% increases together instead of multiplying them.

questions.question_text: Which procedure provides the best evidence about the completeness of trade payables?

options.A: Agreeing a sample of balances on the payables ledger to supporting invoices
options.B: Checking the casting of the payables ledger
options.C: Examining payments made and invoices received after the year end for liabilities that existed at the year end but were not recorded
options.D: Inspecting purchase orders raised after the year end

questions.explanation: A search for unrecorded liabilities looks at transactions after the year end to find amounts that related to the year but were omitted, which tests completeness. Vouching ledger balances tests existence because it starts from recorded items. Casting tests arithmetic, and orders raised after the year end do not represent year-end liabilities.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about a bank confirmation request for audit purposes?

options.A: The request is authorised by the client but sent by the auditor, and the bank replies directly to the auditor
options.B: The request is sent by the client, and the bank replies to the client, who passes the reply to the auditor
options.C: The auditor sends the request without the client's authority
options.D: The bank sends its reply to the client's finance director for checking first

questions.explanation: Banks need the client's authority to disclose information, but the auditor should control the process by sending the request and receiving the reply directly. This prevents the client from intercepting or altering the response and makes the evidence more reliable.

questions.question_text: Which procedure provides the best evidence of the existence of assets recorded in a client's non-current asset register?

options.A: Selecting assets on site and checking they are included in the register
options.B: Recalculating the depreciation charge for the year
options.C: Agreeing the register total to the general ledger
options.D: Selecting assets from the register and physically inspecting them

questions.explanation: Existence is tested by starting from the recorded assets and confirming that they are physically present. Starting from assets on site tests completeness, recalculating depreciation tests valuation, and agreeing totals checks that the register reconciles to the ledger.

questions.question_text: A client's plant and machinery has a cost brought forward of £480,000. Additions in the year cost £60,000 and there were no disposals. The accounting policy is 20% straight-line, with a full year's charge in the year of acquisition. The client has charged depreciation of £102,000. What is the expected charge and what does the comparison show?

options.A: £96,000; the charge is overstated by £6,000
options.B: £102,000; the charge is correct
options.C: £108,000; the charge is understated by £6,000
options.D: £108,000; the charge is overstated by £6,000

questions.explanation: Expected depreciation = (£480,000 + £60,000) x 20% = £540,000 x 20% = £108,000. The client's charge of £102,000 is £6,000 lower, which equals half a year's depreciation on the additions (£60,000 x 20% x 6/12), suggesting a time-apportioned charge was used contrary to policy. £96,000 omits the additions altogether.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT the auditor's responsibility when attending a client's inventory count?

options.A: Observing whether the client's staff follow the count instructions
options.B: Counting all of the inventory and preparing the count sheets for the client
options.C: Performing test counts in both directions between the records and the physical inventory
options.D: Recording details of the last goods received and despatched notes for cut-off testing

questions.explanation: Management is responsible for counting the inventory and preparing the count records. The auditor attends to observe the count, perform test counts, gather cut-off information and note damaged or obsolete items. If the auditor performed the count, this would create a self-review threat and confuse responsibilities.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes analytical procedures?

options.A: Evaluations of financial information through analysis of plausible relationships among both financial and non-financial data
options.B: Checking the arithmetical accuracy of documents and records
options.C: Obtaining written responses directly from third parties
options.D: Examining documents to confirm that transactions were authorised

questions.explanation: Analytical procedures involve comparing figures and ratios with expectations, such as prior years, budgets or industry data, and investigating fluctuations that are unusual. Checking arithmetic is recalculation, third-party responses are external confirmations, and examining documents for authorisation is inspection.

questions.question_text: A company's year end is 31 December. Its last electricity bill covered the period up to 31 October. The next quarterly bill, received in February, was £9,600 for the three months from 1 November to 31 January. What accrual should be recognised at 31 December?
questions.explanation: Two of the three months covered by the bill (November and December) fall within the year. Accrual = £9,600 x 2/3 = £6,400. £9,600 would accrue the whole quarter including January, £3,200 is only one month, and £6,000 would be two-thirds of an estimate of £9,000 rather than the actual bill.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes audit sampling?

options.A: Testing all items above a set value and ignoring the rest of the population
options.B: Selecting the items the auditor considers most interesting
options.C: Testing every item in a population using computer software
options.D: Applying audit procedures to less than 100% of items in a population so that every sampling unit has a chance of selection

questions.explanation: Audit sampling allows the auditor to draw conclusions about a whole population from a selection, provided each unit has a chance of being selected. Testing only high-value items is a targeted approach, not sampling, and leaves the remainder untested. Testing 100% of items is not sampling at all.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of statistical sampling?

options.A: Selection based on the auditor's judgement of which items are most likely to be misstated
options.B: Testing only items processed in the last month of the year
options.C: Selection of items without any defined method
options.D: Random selection of items and the use of probability theory to evaluate the results

questions.explanation: Statistical sampling requires random selection and the use of probability theory to evaluate results, including measuring sampling risk. Any approach without both features is non-statistical. Judgemental selection and selecting only year-end items do not meet these requirements.

questions.question_text: An auditor wishes to select a sample of 60 sales invoices from a population of 2,400 invoices using systematic selection. What is the sampling interval?
questions.explanation: Sampling interval = population size / sample size = 2,400 / 60 = 40. The auditor would choose a random starting point between 1 and 40 and then select every 40th invoice. 60 is the sample size, and 24 and 400 result from misplacing the decimal point.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes haphazard selection?

options.A: The auditor selects items without following a structured technique, while trying to avoid any conscious bias
options.B: Every nth item is selected after a random start
options.C: Items are selected using random number generator software
options.D: Items are selected in proportion to their monetary value

questions.explanation: Haphazard selection involves picking items without a structured method, trying to avoid bias such as always choosing large or easily located items. Because it is not truly random, it is not suitable for statistical sampling. The other options describe systematic, random and monetary unit selection.

questions.question_text: When testing controls, which of the following would increase the required sample size?

options.A: An increase in the tolerable rate of deviation
options.B: A decrease in the level of reliance the auditor plans to place on the control
options.C: An increase in the expected rate of deviation in the population
options.D: An increase in the size of an already large population

questions.explanation: The more deviations the auditor expects to find, the larger the sample needed to conclude that the actual rate does not exceed the tolerable rate. A higher tolerable rate or lower planned reliance reduces the sample size. For large populations, increasing the population size has little effect on sample size.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of non-sampling risk?

options.A: The sample selected happens not to be representative of the population
options.B: The auditor concludes controls are effective when the population deviation rate is higher than in the sample
options.C: The auditor examines a document but fails to recognise a misstatement in it
options.D: The auditor concludes a balance is not materially misstated because the sample contained fewer errors than the population

questions.explanation: Non-sampling risk arises from factors other than sampling, for example using inappropriate procedures or misinterpreting evidence. Sampling risk is the risk that the auditor's conclusion based on a sample differs from the conclusion if the whole population were tested, which the other three options describe.

questions.question_text: An auditor tests a sample of receivables balances with a total value of £50,000 from a population of £800,000. Misstatements found in the sample total £1,500. Using ratio projection, what is the projected misstatement for the population?
questions.explanation: Misstatement rate = £1,500 / £50,000 = 3%. Projected misstatement = 3% x £800,000 = £24,000. £1,500 is only the actual misstatement found and ignores the untested items. £22,500 applies the rate to the untested £750,000 only and omits the misstatement already found in the sample.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of audit documentation?

options.A: To provide the client with a copy of all working papers for its own records
options.B: To provide evidence of the basis for the auditor's conclusions
options.C: To provide evidence that the audit was planned and performed in accordance with auditing standards
options.D: To help the engagement team plan and perform the audit and allow its work to be reviewed

questions.explanation: Audit documentation records the work done, the evidence obtained and the conclusions reached, and supports direction, supervision and review. It belongs to the audit firm and is not prepared for the client's use. Giving the client all working papers could also make future audits predictable.

questions.question_text: Which of the following must be recorded on audit working papers documenting the testing of a sample of purchase invoices?

options.A: The name of every employee who processed each invoice
options.B: Who performed the work and the date, who reviewed it and the date, and identifying characteristics of the invoices tested
options.C: The auditor's opinion on the financial statements as a whole
options.D: The total fee charged for the audit

questions.explanation: Auditing standards require documentation of the identifying characteristics of items tested, who performed and reviewed the work, and when. This allows the work to be reviewed and repeated if needed. Employee names for each invoice, the overall opinion and the audit fee are not required on a working paper for a sample test.

questions.question_text: Who owns the audit working papers prepared during a statutory audit?

options.A: The client company
options.B: The audit firm
options.C: The client's shareholders
options.D: The Registrar of Companies

questions.explanation: Working papers are the property of the audit firm. The firm may make parts of them available to the client at its discretion, provided this does not undermine the independence or effectiveness of the audit. The firm must also keep them confidential and secure.

questions.question_text: After the final audit file has been assembled, the auditor finds it necessary to add new documentation. Which of the following is permitted?

options.A: Deleting earlier working papers that are no longer considered relevant
options.B: Replacing working papers with revised versions without recording the change
options.C: Adding the documentation, provided the auditor records the reasons and when and by whom it was added and reviewed
options.D: Discarding the audit file once the client has accepted the auditor's report
